definition: Two networks — a generator and a discriminator — trained in opposition so the generator learns to create realistic data.
details: The generator tries to fool the discriminator into believing its outputs are real, while the discriminator learns to tell real from fake; the competition drives both to improve. GANs produced startlingly realistic images and remain important in the history of generative models, although diffusion models have since become the dominant image approach.

explainer.lead: A generative adversarial network, or GAN, trains two neural networks against each other: one creates data, and the other judges whether it is real. This contest can teach the creator to produce strikingly realistic images, making GANs an important milestone in generative AI.

tiers.eli5: Imagine an artist trying to draw convincing pictures and a detective trying to spot the artist's fakes. Every time the detective catches one, the artist learns to do better; every time the artist improves, the detective has to sharpen their skills. With enough practice, the artist can produce pictures that look real.
tiers.practitioner: A GAN is trained as a pair: the generator produces candidate data, while the discriminator learns to distinguish those outputs from real examples. The discriminator's real-versus-fake decisions provide the training signal for both networks. GANs can generate highly realistic images, but diffusion models have since become the dominant approach for image generation.
tiers.paperLevel: A GAN comprises a generator G and a discriminator D trained with opposing objectives: G aims to produce outputs that D classifies as real, while D aims to separate real data from G's outputs. Their adversarial training drives the generator toward realistic data. GANs produced notably realistic images, although diffusion models later became dominant for image generation.

explainer.example: A generator creates an image of a face, and the discriminator compares it with real face images and labels it fake. That result helps the generator improve its next image while also giving the discriminator more practice at spotting generated faces.

components.name: Generator
components.detail: Creates candidate data and tries to make it realistic enough to fool the discriminator.

components.name: Discriminator
components.detail: Examines real and generated data and learns to tell them apart.

components.name: Adversarial training
components.detail: Uses the competition between the two networks to drive both to improve.

flow: The discriminator receives generated data and real data.
The discriminator judges whether each input is real or fake.
Those judgments guide improvements to both networks, and the contest repeats.
explainer.lineage: GANs became known for startlingly realistic images and remain important in generative-model history. Diffusion models have since become the dominant approach to image generation.
explainer.whyItMatters: GANs showed that competition between two networks could train a system to generate highly realistic data. They remain a key milestone even as image generation has shifted toward diffusion models.
